sub_unit_name: Classification- solid fuels: coal analysis of coal - proximate and ultimate analysis and their significance

content.title: Solid Fuels
content.description: Solid fuels are combustible solid substances that produce heat energy on burning. Coal is the most widely used solid fuel in domestic, industrial, and power generation sectors.

content.content: Solid fuels are economical, easy to transport and store, and possess good calorific value. Among all solid fuels, coal is the most important fossil fuel used for steam generation, electricity production, metallurgy, and various industrial processes.

content.title: Engineering Importance
content.content: Coal remains one of the major energy sources for thermal power plants, steel industries, cement industries, and boilers.
Solid fuels are broadly classified into natural solid fuels and artificial solid fuels. Natural fuels occur in nature, whereas artificial fuels are prepared by processing natural fuels.

Coal is a black or brown combustible sedimentary rock formed from the decomposition of ancient plant matter under high pressure and temperature over millions of years. It mainly contains carbon along with hydrogen, oxygen, sulphur, nitrogen, and mineral matter.

rows: Hard, highest calorific value, least smoke

content.content: Coal analysis determines the quality, combustion efficiency, suitability for industrial use, storage behavior, and economic value of coal. It helps engineers select appropriate coal for boilers, furnaces, and power plants.

Proximate analysis is a simple method used to determine the percentages of moisture, volatile matter, ash, and fixed carbon present in coal. It provides quick information regarding the combustion characteristics of coal.
Moisture is determined by heating coal at about 105–110°C. High moisture reduces calorific value, increases transportation cost, and lowers combustion efficiency.
Volatile matter is determined by heating coal in the absence of air at about 950°C. High volatile matter makes ignition easier but produces more smoke during combustion.
Ash is the non-combustible inorganic residue left after complete combustion. High ash decreases heating value and causes clinker formation in boilers.
Fixed carbon represents the solid combustible matter remaining after removing moisture, volatile matter, and ash. Higher fixed carbon indicates better fuel quality and higher calorific value.
Ultimate analysis determines the elemental composition of coal, namely carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur, and ash. It is useful for combustion calculations and determining calorific value.

items.question: Carbon
items.answer: Main heat-producing constituent. Higher carbon means higher calorific value.

items.question: Hydrogen
items.answer: Contributes to heat generation but forms water during combustion.

items.question: Oxygen
items.answer: Reduces the effective calorific value of coal.

items.question: Nitrogen
items.answer: Does not contribute to heating and may form harmful oxides.

items.question: Sulphur
items.answer: Produces SO₂ causing corrosion and air pollution.

items.question: Ash
items.answer: Reduces fuel efficiency and increases maintenance cost.

items.question: Boiler Performance
items.answer: Helps select suitable coal for efficient boiler operation.

items.question: Fuel Quality
items.answer: Quickly indicates the combustion quality of coal.

items.question: Storage
items.answer: Moisture information helps in proper storage.

items.question: Industrial Selection
items.answer: Used for selecting coal for furnaces and power plants.

items.question: Calorific Value
items.answer: Used in Dulong's formula for calculating HCV.

items.question: Air Requirement
items.answer: Helps determine theoretical oxygen needed for combustion.

items.question: Pollution Control
items.answer: Sulphur and nitrogen estimation helps reduce emissions.

items.question: Combustion Design
items.answer: Useful in designing furnaces and combustion systems.

content.title: Exam Tip
content.content: Differentiate proximate and ultimate analysis clearly. Questions frequently ask the parameters determined in each analysis and their significance.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Coal is the most important solid fossil fuel.
Solid fuels are classified as natural and artificial.
Coal is classified into peat, lignite, bituminous, and anthracite.
Proximate analysis determines moisture, volatile matter, ash, and fixed carbon.
Ultimate analysis determines carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur, and ash.
Moisture and ash reduce fuel efficiency.
Higher fixed carbon and carbon content indicate better quality coal.
Ultimate analysis is useful for combustion calculations and calorific value estimation.
